teams.heading: Jiuta Wainiqolo creates all three Fiji tries in 23-21 loss to Italy
teams.body: Italy won Friday's 11th-place final at Twickenham 23-21, but Fiji's attack ran through their right wing. Wainiqolo's long cut-out pass put Ponipate Loganimasi away for Fiji's first try. He sent fellow wing Peniasi Dakuwaqa over after the break, then released No. 8 Kitione Salawa on 55 minutes to edge Jake White's side 21-20 ahead. Fiji outscored Italy three tries to two, yet Tommaso Allan landed all five goal kicks, the last coming after Fiji conceded a scrum penalty on the edge of their own 22.

lead.why: The result has already run, so this leads on a new Fiji angle from the match report: Wainiqolo created every Fiji try in the defeat.

teams.heading: England Rugby mourns former scrum-half Nigel Starmer-Smith, who has died aged 81
teams.body: The Harlequins and Barbarians scrum-half made seven England appearances between 1969 and 1971. After retiring in 1976 he moved into broadcasting and commentated at the 2003 World Cup in Australia. He was diagnosed with dementia in 2015, and his son Charlie said he died peacefully on Thursday morning after a long battle with the condition, remembering him as “one of life’s great tourists.”

teams.heading: France release 14 players to Top 14 and name five final reservists
teams.body: The five reservists for Sunday's final against South Africa are Moses Alo Emile, Esteban Capilla, Guillaume Cramont, Paul Graou and Thomas Laclayat, leaving Bayonne without Capilla and Cramont against Castres. The 14 cut loose midweek are all free for round 10 of the Top 14. Rodrigue Neti and Joshua Brennan were already training with Toulouse on Wednesday, Gaël Dréan and Mathis Ferté could boost Toulon at Clermont, and Nicolas Depoortère can line up for Bordeaux-Bègles against Montpellier.

lead.why: A fresh France selection decision on the squad for the final; the Ramos recall and 6-2 bench have already run.

teams.heading: James McNabney scores twice as Ireland beat Australia 38-14 at Twickenham
teams.body: Ireland closed the inaugural Nations Championship in fifth place with a 38-14 win over the Wallabies at Twickenham on Friday. James McNabney, off the bench for only his second cap, crossed twice in the final seven minutes. Andy Farrell's side trailed 7-0 after a sloppy opening quarter before Robbie Henshaw, Nick Timoney and Rob Baloucoune scored. Sam Prendergast kicked six from six and set up Baloucoune with a cross-kick. The result completed a clean sweep of four November Tests.

lead.why: Ireland's result against Australia is the fresh event, and McNabney's two tries off the bench are the talking point.

teams.heading: Tommaso Allan kicks Italy past Fiji 23-21 to end seven-match losing run
teams.body: Friday's 11th-place final at Twickenham went Italy's way 23-21, ending a seven-match losing run and avenging last week's 21-16 defeat in Udine. Federico Mori and Giacomo Nicotera crossed for a 17-0 lead before Fiji, outscoring Italy three tries to two, went 21-20 up on 55 minutes. Allan landed all five goal kicks, the last a 68th-minute penalty, and the defence held. Ross Vintcent took player of the match with a joint match-high 17 tackles.

lead.why: Italy's first win since March is the day's fresh event and hasn't been reported yet.

teams.heading: Scotland finish fourth in Northern Hemisphere table after Ireland stun South Africa
teams.body: Townsend's side ended the pool phase on 20 points. The 11 tries in their 67-5 rout of Japan were not enough to keep them out of a seventh-place play-off at Twickenham. Their autumn also brought a gruelling 15-12 win over Australia at Murrayfield and a 43-21 defeat by the All Blacks. Argentina, beaten 47-38 by Scotland in Córdoba in July, finished fourth in the Southern Hemisphere standings, with ranking points and the Hemisphere Shield still at stake.

teams.heading: Sam Costelow starts at fly-half against Japan having risen above online abuse
teams.body: The Scarlets man has the No. 10 shirt for today's ninth-place final at Allianz Stadium, and WalesOnline argues he has earned it the hard way. Thrust into the starting XV straight after the 2023 World Cup, Costelow was dropped by Warren Gatland after one match, then spent two years in and out as Ben Thomas and Gareth Anscombe moved ahead of him. Online criticism turned vitriolic at times, as it once did for Rhys Priestland; over the past 18 months he has pushed Dan Edwards hard for the jersey.

lead.why: The only new Wales story not already run: Costelow's hard road to the No. 10 shirt he wears against Japan.

teams.heading: Contepomi starts Isgró and Sánchez Valarolo, moves Scelzo to No. 8
teams.body: Rodrigo Isgró takes Bautista Delguy's wing for Sunday's seventh-place final at Twickenham, while the 22-year-old Sánchez Valarolo comes in at inside centre for Justo Piccardo, who drops to the bench. Joaquín Moro starts at openside, with Scelzo shifting across from seven and Facundo Isa dropping out. Up front, prop Martínez replaces the injured Boris Wenger. Gregor Townsend reckons the Pumas have become much more aggressive with their line speed over recent games, hitting hard and putting bodies into contact.

teams.heading: Wasteful Wallabies beaten 38-14 by Ireland, a seventh straight loss to them
teams.body: Australia's year closed with a 38-14 loss in Friday's Nations Championship fifth-place final at Allianz Stadium, where dominant early pressure brought only Jeremy Williams' try. Ireland then ran in 24 unanswered points either side of half-time, and replacement James McNabney's late double extended their winning run over the Wallabies to seven. Kalani Thomas scored his first Test try on his first start, while Max Jorgensen departed with a failed HIA. Captain Allan Alaalatoa admitted the side "probably hurt ourselves a little bit through our discipline in giving them easy exits."

lead.why: The 38-14 defeat is the fresh Australia event, and the previous editions covered only pre-match selection.

teams.heading: Dylan Riley leaves Japan camp for birth of his son before Wales
teams.body: Riley's absence, confirmed this week, deepens a selection squeeze for Saturday's ninth-place final against Wales. Ryosuke Iwaihara and Seina Kimura were both ruled out after Scotland's 67-5 win, and Rugby Asia 247 notes several players have dropped out of contention since Wales beat Japan 28-21 in round four. Eddie Jones' depleted side arrive on a four-match losing streak, having conceded 261 points and 40 tries in the pool stage — the worst defensive record in either hemisphere.

lead.why: Riley's departure and two fresh casualties are Japan's own availability news, separate from the selection story already run, while the only NEW item is Wales'.

teams.heading: Jeff Wilson backs under-fire defence coach Tana Umaga over missed tackles
teams.body: New Zealand have shipped 10 tries in the defeats to Wales and England — five apiece — and conceded more than 30 points five times this season, drawing fire on the former captain who runs the defence. Wilson told Sport Nation that "the 32 tackles that were missed last weekend aren't Tana's fault," also pointing to injury-driven selection churn among the outside backs. He insisted a coaching change is not yet warranted, though only a really poor showing in today's third-place final against England could change that conversation.

lead.why: The captaincy and drug-testing stories have already run, and Umaga's defence is the most pointed New Zealand story left on the shortlist.

teams.heading: Marco van Staden banned for three matches over Tadhg Beirne cleanout
teams.body: Friday's judicial verdict came six days after Ireland beat the Springboks 20-17 in Dublin. Rassie Erasmus had already left the back-rower out of his 23 for Sunday's final against France without knowing the outcome. Van Staden's late yellow for a dangerous cleanout on Beirne was upgraded to red after the final whistle. The ban was mitigated down from six and drops to two if he completes World Rugby's coaching intervention programme. Jasper Wiese, banned for four weeks for another dangerous breakdown entry, also misses the final.

lead.why: A fresh disciplinary ruling on a Springbok forward is today's new South Africa event, and it confirms a second loose forward out of the final.
